final.investment_thesis:
This resolves to Hold not because the debate is a tie, but because each side wins a different question and the winner on each question forbids a different action.

The bull wins the fundamentals exchange, and the record is not close. AAPL printed Q3 FY26 revenue of $109.42B (+16.4%), a record 50.06% gross margin (+357 bps), EPS +28.7% to $2.02, 9M FCF of $110.20B (+52.5%), net cash of $62.22B versus $33.74B a year ago, debt/equity down from 1.34x to 0.78x, and a current ratio above 1.0 for the first time in the dataset. Price sits 9.93% above a rising 200-day at 281.90 and only 0.31% below the 50-day, 0.51% below the Bollinger middle and 0.12% below the 10-EMA — with ATR at 7.23 points, all three gaps sit inside a single normal session. Volume into the drift contracted from 50.51M to 25.87M, which is more consistent with absence of supply than with heavy-volume distribution, and VWMA has ticked up four sessions to 309.19. A 0.96-point gap to the 50-day cannot be called a trend break when the stock routinely travels 7 points.

The bear nevertheless wins the two points that govern the marginal dollar, which is why nothing is added. First, valuation: at 14.594B shares and $309.90 AAPL is a ~$4.52T company at ~34x FY26 EPS with roughly a 2.8% clean FCF yield once the $15–16B working-capital benefit the bull himself concedes is stripped out — the bull cannot concede the cash flow is overstated and then cite the overstated figure to argue cheapness. Second, margin durability is genuinely unresolved: raw materials rose +260% to $7,645M and total inventory +94%, which is either a forward hedge or $7.6B of inventory laid in ahead of a confirmed memory cost shock flowing through COGS over two to four quarters; Q3 ended June 27, so Q3 COGS does not settle it. The only forward-looking mix proxy — deferred revenue +4.3% against revenue +16% — leans against the high-margin Services-mix story, and with no segment tags, no unit volumes and no attribution for the 7/31 gap, neither side can claim the margin attribution it needs. The buyback 'anchor' is weaker than presented: $62.094B / 164.3M net retirements is an upper bound inflated by the net-retirement artifact, the report's own band is $300–380 (27% wide, no margin of safety at $310), the program is explicitly price-insensitive, and repurchases decelerated 12% while FCF rose 52.5% — a flow, not a valuation signal. The bull's own risk/reward only works at spot with a 300 stop, not at his stated 321 entry against a 310 stop, where reward-to-risk to his first target is under 1:1.

What that means operationally is that both analysts converge on the same structure: a 302–317 coil under an unrecovered gap, with 320.28 (8/20 rejection high) as the upside trigger ~3.3% away and 300.00 (7/31 low, held 17 sessions through five tests) as the invalidation ~3.2% away — each roughly 1.4 ATR. Neither has fired. The upside case is real but unconfirmed; the downside case is real but unconfirmed, and the floor has held. The bear's conclusion was 'do not initiate ahead of 320.28,' not 'exit.' So the bear's valuation and margin-durability work blocks any add, and the bull's balance sheet, record margin and 17-session floor block any liquidation.

On sizing, the three risk seats converge on 1.99% retained, and I adopt it while correcting the reasoning two of them used. The conservative seat treats it as a 'minimum tolerated exposure' and the neutral seat goes further, calling it an economically functionless position kept only by fee inertia and correctly noting that observation does not require shares. The neutral analyst is right that observation is free; they are wrong that this is what the position is for. The position is a defined-risk claim: with invalidation 3.2% away at a level tested five times in 17 sessions and the July congestion 7.5–9.7% above, the loss side is bounded and pre-identified while the gain side is not — ~$180 of downside to 281.90 and ~$220 of upside to 344.57, each ~0.2% of total equity. At 1.99% a full drop to the 200-day (−9.0%) costs ~0.18% of total equity. That asymmetry at a size where error is nearly free is worth the ~$2 of round-trip fees. The aggressive seat is right that zero exposure also forfeits upside, but their symmetry argument is not what carries the day; the concrete cost is re-entry. Exiting to 0% and then adding only on a 320.28 confirmation on volume >50M would mean buying a future 4–5% position (~$4,000) roughly 3.3% higher, or ~$130 of give-up, against ~$2 saved in fees — that is the trade being rejected, not a sentiment preference.

The higher alternative of ~5.0% was weighed and rejected. It would put ~$4,995 at risk, raise total-equity gain to ~0.55% on a move to 344.57 versus ~0.22% today, and that forgone ~0.33% is the explicit price of waiting. I pay it because Q4 FY26 is a gross-margin-guided binary print inside a week flagged for Nvidia earnings and Jackson Hole, because the 50-day has been flat for three weeks, and because MACD remains below zero at −1.4389 versus a −1.29032 signal with a decelerating histogram — adding now exposes the full stake to whipsaw through a 0.3-ATR four-way average confluence (50-SMA 310.88, Bollinger middle 311.50, 10-EMA 310.27, VWMA 309.19) that the aggressive analyst himself concedes offers no directional information. The lower alternative of 0% was also weighed and rejected for the re-entry arithmetic above: zero exposure buys nothing that watching the 320.28 and 300.00 prints does not already give, while converting a bounded claim into a decision to pay up later.

Prior outcomes shape this. The 08-17 and 08-12 Underweight reflections established that when distance-to-invalidation is small relative to distance-to-confirmation, a directional rating has poor expectancy — here those distances are nearly equal (3.2% down versus 3.3% up), which is precisely the configuration that argues for Hold rather than a directional expression. The 08-14 Overweight reflection argued for pre-committing more size when risk is bounded by arithmetic rather than tape; that does not apply yet, because at 08-14 the floor was immediate and the position established, whereas now price sits mid-coil and the decisive variable is an unquantified Q4 gross-margin guide. The 08-18 Hold reflection supplies the judging rule: pre-commit to re-underwriting at the print rather than reading a flat five-day window as evidence. My own repeated AAPL Underweights on momentum decay inside an intact uptrend (07-20 through 07-24, 07-31, 08-11, 08-17) each bled 2.1% to 13.6% of five-day alpha, and the 08-24 realized loss of −$111.00 with $27.92 of cumulative fees is the reminder that churn at this size costs more than it protects.

What would change it. Toward ~4–5%: a daily close above 320.28 on volume >50M shares, MACD crossing above zero, and a Q4 FY26 gross-margin guide at or above 49.5% with revenue growth at or above 12% — all three, not any one. Toward 0%: a daily close below 300.00 on expanding volume, with 293.39 (lower Bollinger) and 281.90 (200-day, a further −9.0%) as downstream references, at which point the bear's margin-durability thesis becomes operative. These are narrative conditions only, not implemented stops or orders; each requires a fresh review on the signal day.

Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment disclosure, no unit volumes, no attribution for the 7/31 gap, no segment-level Services margin, and no vendor price multiples — the ~34x P/E and ~2.8% clean FCF yield are arithmetic on supplied inputs (14.594B shares, ~$9.05 FY26 EPS, ~$126B annualized clean FCF), not vendor-reported. News coverage is partial, with no items supplied for 8/18–8/22. Cash earns no interest, the next-open price is unknown, and the 10-bps fee argues against unnecessary transactions — which is why the correct action today is none.
final.time_horizon: 1–3 months; re-underwritten at the Q4 FY26 print or on resolution of 320.28 / 300.00
